correctness.rationale: Complete independent face enumeration (24,204,744,1116,528,32), verified acyclic 1287-pair matching over all 9936 incidences, and signed 65-by-8 critical attaching matrix with explicit -I8 minor prove the homotopy type. The unique 0-cell and lack of 1,2-cells give a wedge of 65 three-spheres as skeleton; Hurewicz and primitive independent attachments cancel eight of them. Standalone programs independently check mod-two ranks 23,181,563,496,32 but those ranks are not substituted for integral proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The cuboctahedron is planar but not outerplanar, since any simple outerplanar graph on 12 vertices has at most 21 edges while C has 24. Its minimum degree is four and the polyhedral cycles do not form a polygonal line with degree-two end vertices. Matsushita treats ladder-strip-derived Δ graphs, not this regular double line graph. Engström gives connectivity criteria rather than a graph-specific integral homotopy decomposition. None of these theorems implies a rank-57 three-sphere wedge for the present object.

value.rationale: The ordinary matching complex of a canonical Archimedean 4-regular planar graph resolves a natural graph-topology invariant beyond the outerplanar wedge theorem, explicitly contributing one positive nonouterplanar instance to the stated conjecture for planar graphs. The integral unimodular cellular computation supplies a full exact homotopy type and rules out torsion or higher attaching-map obstructions; this precise invariant is not implied by graph parameters or mod-two Betti counts.
